findings.reason: parser.ts:1105-1113 builds the same {type, start, anchor*, tag*, style} literal that addMappingEvent and insertFlowPairMappingEvent also build, so the shape is duplicated. The behaviour matches the old code: position is already past ':' after line 1096, the line didn't change, and the event lands at beforeKey.eventsLength. So this is only maintainability debt and stays low.
findings.claim: The block MAPPING event is built as an inline object literal in splice, making a third copy of the event shape next to addMappingEvent (line 131) and insertFlowPairMappingEvent (line 151).
findings.evidence: Lines 1105-1113 call `state.events.splice(beforeKey.eventsLength, 0, { type: EVENT_ID.MAPPING, start: beforeKey.position, anchorStart: props.anchorStart, ... style: COLLECTION_STYLE.BLOCK })`. insertFlowPairMappingEvent (line 151) already does the same splice-at-snapshot, but it hard-codes NO_RANGE properties and FLOW style. addMappingEvent (line 131) builds the same object but pushes it instead of inserting it. I traced the logic and found it equivalent to the removed restore-and-reparse path: position ends just past ':', the event lands at index beforeKey.eventsLength as the callers at lines 1225 and 1289 expect, and `ch` is reassigned at line 1154 before it is read again. So this is maintainability debt only. Generalising insertFlowPairMappingEvent to take props and style would remove the copy.
